added.description:
Who You'll Work With

Driving lasting impact and building long-term capabilities with our clients is not easy work. You are the kind of person who thrives in a high performance/high reward culture - doing hard things, picking yourself up when you stumble, and having the resilience to try another way forward.

In return for your drive, determination, and curiosity, we'll provide the resources, mentorship, and opportunities you need to become a stronger leader faster than you ever thought possible. Your colleagues—at all levels—will invest deeply in your development, just as much as they invest in delivering exceptional results for clients. Every day, you'll receive apprenticeship, coaching, and exposure that will accelerate your growth in ways you won’t find anywhere else.

When you join us, you will have:

Continuous learning: Our learning and apprenticeship culture, backed by structured programs, is all about helping you grow while creating an environment where feedback is clear, actionable, and focused on your development. The real magic happens when you take the input from others to heart and embrace the fast-paced learning experience, owning your journey.
A voice that matters: From day one, we value your ideas and contributions. You’ll make a tangible impact by offering innovative ideas and practical solutions, all while upholding our unwavering commitment to ethics and integrity. We not only encourage diverse perspectives, but they are critical in driving us toward the best possible outcomes.
Global community: With colleagues across 65+ countries and over 100 different nationalities, our firm’s diversity fuels creativity and helps us come up with the best solutions for our clients. Plus, you’ll have the opportunity to learn from exceptional colleagues with diverse backgrounds and experiences.
World-class benefits: On top of a competitive salary (based on your location, experience, and skills), we provide a comprehensive benefits package to enable holistic well-being for you and your family.

Your Impact

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll deploy and scale EcliptOS— QuantumBlack's AI forward Operating System — a next-generation platform designed to connect strategy to execution through agentic systems.

This role sits at the intersection of software engineering and infrastructure, bringing EcliptOS into real-world environments and ensuring it works at scale. You'll play a key role in how the platform is deployed, adopted, and operated, enabling organizations to translate complex AI strategies into practical, high-impact solutions.

You'll own the EcliptOS platform delivery lifecycle, bridging product engineering and client environments. Responsibilities include deploying and configuring production-grade systems across cloud and hybrid infrastructures (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), validating performance and stability, and ensuring structured handovers for long-term success. Work often involves containerized and distributed systems, including Kubernetes-based environments, where reliability and operational stability are critical. You'll troubleshoot issues end-to-end and ensure EcliptOS is fully production-ready, while also contributing to deployment tooling, automation, and product feedback loops to improve platform reliability and delivery.

The impact of this work is tangible. You'll enable clients to run AI-driven workflows and manage intelligent systems within their existing technology ecosystems. Working closely with technical stakeholders, you'll ensure environment readiness, resolve deployment challenges, and guide adoption through practical best practices. Your experience from the field will also contribute to feedback loops between deployments and EcliptOS product development, supporting the continuous evolution of QuantumBlack's technology.

Based in one of our North America offices, you'll work closely with engineers, product teams, and technical experts across QuantumBlack's global community. Beyond EcliptOS deployments, you'll collaborate with data scientists, machine learning engineers, designers, and technologists on interdisciplinary initiatives, contributing to a broader ecosystem of AI innovation. Together, you'll help operationalize advanced AI systems across industries, driving successful delivery, validation, and adoption in client environments. You'll also contribute to team knowledge-sharing — documenting patterns, refining delivery practices, and supporting colleagues across engagements.

At QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, you'll thrive in an unparalleled environment for growth. You'll develop a sought-after perspective by connecting technology and business value, work across industries, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to unlock the transformative potential of AI, while advancing as a technologist and leader.

Your Qualifications and Skills

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science, machine learning, applied statistics, mathematics, engineering, artificial intelligence, or a related field
4+ years of hands-on experience as a Software or Platform Engineer, with exposure to enterprise platform deployments
Strong engineering fundamentals with proficiency in Python and familiarity with modern full-stack development (e.g., React, NextJS or equivalent)
Experience designing, deploying, and managing cloud-based systems (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including containerization (Docker) and orchestration frameworks, with hands-on experience operating and troubleshooting production systems
Deep expertise in Kubernetes cluster architecture, installation, configuration, and lifecycle management at production scale
Experience with CI/CD pipelines and Infrastructure as Code (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Terraform, Ansible, Helm)
Strong understanding of data architectures and platform design, including relational and graph databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, Neo4j), data pipelines, and system integration patterns across structured and unstructured data
Familiarity with AI platform concepts, including model integration patterns, agentic workflows, and how AI-driven applications interact with underlying data and infrastructure is a plus
Strong problem-solving skills with a structured approach to debugging and resolving issues in complex, non-standard environments
Experience with DevSecOps and infrastructure security practices (e.g., IAM/SSO, RBAC, secrets management, encryption) is a plus
Experience with deployment standards, runbook development, and automation frameworks is a strong advantage
Familiarity with observability, monitoring, and compliance tooling (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, ELK) and experience working in secure or regulated environments is a plus.
Willingness to travel
Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders in client-facing settings, including delivering walkthroughs, documentation, and training

Job Description

Are you passionate about harnessing the power of artificial intelligence and machine learning to solve real-world challenges? At JPMorganChase, we're transforming the way payments work in the Commercial & Investment Bank by leveraging cutting-edge document extraction and natural language processing (NLP) technologies. As a Vice President and Applied AI/ML Lead, you'll play a pivotal role in building innovative solutions that enhance trust, safety, and operational efficiency for one of the world's leading financial institutions.

As a Vice President, Applied AI and Machine Learning Lead at JPMorganChase within Payments Technology in the Commercial & Investment Bank
, you will lead the delivery of document extraction and natural language processing capabilities that improve trust, safety, and operational effectiveness. You will own solutions end-to-end, from problem framing and data strategy to production deployment and measurement. You will remain hands-on while setting technical direction and partnering across product, engineering, data, risk, and compliance stakeholders.

Job Responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery of document extraction and natural language processing solutions, from opportunity sizing and requirements through production rollout and iteration.
Design scalable model pipelines for document ingestion, text extraction, classification, and ranking, balancing accuracy, latency, throughput, and cost.
Develop and improve natural language processing algorithms and model approaches to extract entities, relationships, and signals from unstructured text and documents.
Define evaluation strategies and success metrics, including offline validation, error analysis, robustness testing, and controlled online measurement where appropriate.
Establish model lifecycle practices including reproducibility, testing, monitoring, drift detection, and incident response to sustain reliable production performance.
Partner with risk and compliance stakeholders to ensure appropriate documentation, controls, explainability expectations, and audit-ready processes.
Drive technical decisions through design reviews, code and model reviews, and pragmatic standards that raise quality and delivery velocity.
Communicate tradeoffs and recommendations to senior stakeholders, translating model behavior into decision-ready business impact.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

Formal training or certification on applied artificial intelligence and machine learning concepts and 5+ years applied experience
5+ years of experience building and delivering applied machine learning or natural language processing solutions with measurable outcomes in production.
Strong programming skills in Python and experience using modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Hands-on experience with document extraction and natural language processing techniques including text classification and information extraction.
Experience designing data-driven solutions using SQL and distributed processing tools such as Spark or equivalent.
Experience deploying and operating machine learning services or pipelines in a cloud environment such as Amazon Web Services (or equivalent).
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into structured machine learning plans, including data strategy, evaluation, rollout, and operationalization.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to technical and non-technical partners.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

Experience with optical character recognition and document understanding workflows for scanned or semi-structured documents.
Experience with modern natural language processing architectures such as transformer-based models and techniques for optimization and efficient inference.
Experience with machine learning operations practices and tooling, including model registries, continuous integration and delivery for machine learning, and observability.
Experience with real-time or event-driven architectures supporting low-latency inference and feature generation.
Experience applying document extraction or natural language processing in payments, financial services, or regulated environments.

added.title: GenAI Inference Engineer (Intelligence Lab)
added.description:
About Us:

webAI is pioneering the future of artificial intelligence by establishing the first distributed AI infrastructure dedicated to personalized AI. We recognize the evolving demands of a data driven society for scalability and flexibility, and we firmly believe that the future of AI lies in distributed processing at the edge, bringing computation closer to the source of data generation.

Our mission is to build a future where a company's valuable data and intellectual property remain entirely private, enabling the deployment of large-scale AI models directly on standard consumer hardware without compromising the information embedded within those models. We are developing an end-to-end platform that is secure, scalable, and fully under the control of our users, empowering enterprises with AI that understands their unique business. We are a team driven by truth, ownership, tenacity, and humility, and we seek individuals who resonate with these core values and are passionate about shaping the next generation of AI.

About the Role:

The webAI Intelligence Lab (WIL) is looking for an AI Software Engineer with deep expertise in high-performance computing and machine learning inference. The AI Engineer is the "builder" who makes the science real. They take raw models and turn them into scalable, efficient, and reliable software. They are the masters of the production environment focusing on latency, reliability, and data integrity.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who thrives at the intersection of low-level systems programming, applied machine learning, and hardware-aware optimization.

Key Responsibilities

Optimization: Implement techniques like pruning, quantization, and distillation to ensure models run efficiently on edge devices or in high-traffic cloud environments.
Model Deployment: Wrap models in high-performance APIs and integrate them into the broader software ecosystem.
Inference Engines: Build and maintain ML frameworks that enable the AI Scientist’s experiments at scale.
Collaboration: Work closely with the AI Scientist to refactor "research code" into production-grade, maintainable code.

Requirements & Skills

Experience: 5+ years in Software Engineering or equivalent university time with a deep experience that matches WIL objectives to include with a focus on ML-specific systems and distributed computing.
Technical Depth: Proficiency in C++/Python, Docker/Kubernetes, Vector Databases (Pinecone, Weaviate), and CI/CD for ML.
Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science or Software Engineering.

We at webAI are committed to living out the core values
we have put in place as the foundation on which we operate as a team. We seek individuals who exemplify the following:

Truth - Emphasizing transparency and honesty in every interaction and decision.
Ownership - Taking full responsibility for one’s actions and decisions, demonstrating commitment to the success of our clients.
Tenacity - Persisting in the face of challenges and setbacks, continually striving for excellence and improvement.
Humility - Maintaining a respectful and learning-oriented mindset, acknowledging the strengths and contributions of others.

Benefits:

We strive to provide competitive benefits to all employees. The benefits listed in this posting generally apply to U.S.-based employees. For employees hired outside the United States, benefits may vary based on local law, country-specific requirements, and the employment platform or entity through which the employee is hired.

401k match (US-based only)

Parental leave for eligible employees
Continuing education support
Basic, company-paid life insurance
Supplemental life insurance
Company-paid short and long term disability
Free parking for in-office employees

added.title: AI Engineer
added.description:
About Distyl AI

Distyl is an applied AI technology company partnering with the world’s most ambitious institutions to rearchitect critical operations for the frontier of AI. Our customers include the largest companies in telecom, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing, consumer goods, and global social organizations.

We research and deploy technologies that power AI-native operations — both for our partners and for Distyl itself. Our work spans research into self-constructing systems, the development of the most reliable execution of AI systems, and products that transform mission-critical workflows. As a result, Distyl's technologies affect some of the world's largest operations — from hundreds of millions of consumer interactions to tens of millions of supply chain transactions and millions of patient journeys.

Distyl is backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Coatue, DST Global, and the board-members of 20+ F500s.

What We Are Looking For

AI Engineers build and operate production AI systems that deliver business value inside customer environments. This role is for engineers who thrive in ambiguous problem spaces, take ownership of outcomes, and want to work directly on AI systems that must perform reliably under enterprise constraints.

AI Engineers are hands-on builders. They design, implement, deploy, and iterate on end-to-end AI systems in close partnership with customers, subject matter experts, and other Distyl engineers. They translate messy operational needs into concrete system behavior, build the software and AI workflows required to support that behavior, and continuously improve systems through evaluation, feedback, integration, and production iteration.

This is not a demo-building role. AI Engineers are expected to make AI systems work in practice: with users, data, constraints, and accountability for production outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Build and operate AI systems deployed in customer environments, taking ownership of system behavior, reliability, and usefulness in production
Design and implement compound AI workflows that combine models, prompts, agents, tools, retrieval, evaluation, feedback loops, and execution into coherent production systems aligned with user and SME needs
Develop clean, maintainable Python services and application logic that integrate AI capabilities into customer workflows, data platforms, APIs, and existing applications
Operate on live systems by measuring behavior, identifying failure modes, debugging issues, and iterating rapidly to improve quality, reliability, and user value
Build evaluation frameworks, test cases, feedback mechanisms, and observability patterns that help teams understand and improve AI system performance over time
Work directly with customer stakeholders and subject matter experts to understand workflows, clarify requirements, reason about tradeoffs, and adapt systems as needs evolve
Use AI-native engineering tools to accelerate implementation, debugging, experimentation, data analysis, and system improvement
Collaborate with other AI Engineers, AI Strategists, and other Distillers to make pragmatic system design decisions that balance speed, robustness, maintainability, and customer impact
Take accountability for the production outcomes of the components, workflows, and systems you build

What We Require

5+ years of software engineering experience
Ownership mentality for AI systems. You take responsibility for whether the systems you build deliver their intended value in production. You are comfortable making technical decisions, learning from system behavior, and owning the results of your work
Experience building AI systems. You have built applications powered by LLMs or other AI models and are comfortable composing multiple components — prompts, agents, tools, retrieval, evaluators, workflows, and integrations — into end-to-end systems. You reason about system behavior holistically rather than treating models as black boxes
Strong engineering fundamentals. You write clean, maintainable Python and are comfortable building production software systems. You understand core engineering concepts like versioning, debugging, testing, performance, code review, and production readiness
AI-native working style. You use AI tools daily to write and debug code, explore designs, analyze data, and automate repetitive work. You are curious about new model capabilities and techniques, and actively incorporate them into how you build and iterate on systems
Comfort in customer environments. You are able to work directly with customer teams, ask good questions, and adapt quickly to new domains. You communicate clearly about system behavior, limitations, and tradeoffs, and can operate effectively in high-trust, high-visibility situations
Pragmatic delivery mindset. You can navigate ambiguity, make progress with incomplete information, and balance speed with robustness when building systems that need to work for production users
Willingness to travel. Travel is typically 10–30%, depending on the project, customer needs, and your role on the engagement

What We Offer

The base salary range for this role is $180K – $250K, depending on experience, location, and level. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for meaningful equity, along with a comprehensive benefits package
100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents
Flexible time off
Retirement and financial planning benefits, including access to pre-tax HSA, FSA, and commuter accounts, 401(k), and financial coaching resources
Comprehensive wellness benefits, including physical fitness, mental well-being, and fertility and family-building benefits through Carrot
Complimentary in-office lunches and snacks provided
Access to state-of-the-art AI models, generous usage of modern AI tools, and real-world business problems
Ownership of high-impact projects across top enterprises
A mission-driven, fast-moving culture that values curiosity, pragmatism, and excellence

Distyl has offices in San Francisco and New York. This role follows a hybrid collaboration model with 3+ days per week (Tuesday–Thursday) in‑office.

We believe diverse perspectives make our work stronger and more impactful. We are an equal opportunity employer and evaluate all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

We're partnering with an exciting, venture-backed AI technology company in New York City that's transforming how accounting firms operate through intelligent automation.

who thrives on solving real-world problems, building production-ready AI solutions and working directly with customers.

added.title: Founding Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
added.description:
Location:
Palo Alto, CA (5 days/week in office)

Type: Full-time
YOE: 2yr+ FDE experiences. (Bonus) technical sales, technical consultant or AI/SaaS founder experience
Compensation: competitive base + equity

About Us

We're building toward a world where every company can become its own AI lab.

Goaly is an early-stage AI startup founded by ex-Meta Superintelligence Labs engineers and researchers. Our founders built the Llama Research Platform that every Llama post-training run landed on, and led post-training efficiency on Meta's Superintelligence team. Our mission is to dramatically lower the cost, time, and talent barriers to building proprietary AI — and make each generation of models faster and cheaper to build than the last.

Goaly is the autonomous performance layer for AI training. It watches every job across a GPU fleet, catches the runs that are wasting compute, reallocates what it frees up, and shows teams what each model improvement actually costs. It runs on-prem, telemetry-only, and starts read-only.

Backed by leading AI investors and endorsed by frontier AI researchers and builders, we're looking for an engineer who can walk into a prospect's GPU cluster, get Goaly running, and prove its value fast enough that the pilot becomes a contract.

We’re building toward a world where every company can become its own AI lab.

Goaly is a stealth AI startup founded by ex-Meta MSL engineers and researchers. Our mission is to dramatically lower the cost, time, and talent barriers to building proprietary AI — and make each generation of models faster and cheaper to build than the last.

Backed by leading AI investors and endorsed by frontier AI researchers and builders, we’re looking for exceptional new grads who want to work on hard, foundational AI systems problems with outsized ownership from day one.

About The Role

You will be one of our first Forward Deployed Engineers, working directly with the founding team. Your job is to shorten the path from "interesting first call" to "signed customer." You will own three things:

Run technical evaluations that close. Scope, deploy, and run Goaly pilots inside prospect environments, and turn each one into a clear, numbers-backed result the buyer can take to their leadership.
Be the technical voice in the deal. Join discovery and evaluation calls, answer the hard infrastructure and security questions on the spot, and remove the blockers that stall deals.
Bring the field back into the product. Turn what you see in real clusters into integrations, fixes, and product changes, so every next deployment is faster than the last.

You need strong systems engineering skills, because you will work inside other people's infrastructure with limited access and real constraints. You need customer instincts, because the job is to make the prospect successful first and Goaly successful as a result. You do not need a background in model research.

This is a founding role. There is no playbook yet; you help write it, and the deployment process you build becomes how Goaly scales to every customer after you.

What you'll do

Deploy Goaly in prospect environments

Scope each pilot with the prospect: which clusters, which workloads, what success looks like, and how we will measure it.
Install and configure Goaly on-prem across the stacks our customers run (Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and in-house schedulers), in read-only, telemetry-only mode.
Work through security reviews, network constraints, and access approvals with the prospect's platform and security teams.
Debug what breaks in real environments: odd scheduler setups, missing metrics, custom training stacks.

Prove the value and convert

Turn pilot data into a clear business case: compute wasted, compute recovered, and the cost of each model improvement.
Present results to ML leads, infra leads, and the executives who sign.
Partner with GTM on deal strategy, technical objections, and the path from pilot to paid deployment.
Keep each evaluation on a tight timeline, and flag early when a deal is at risk.

Build What The Field Needs

Write the integrations, scripts, and connectors that a deployment needs, and push the reusable ones back into the product.
Build and maintain demo environments and reference deployments for sales calls.
Turn repeated questions into docs, runbooks, and install guides, so time-to-value drops with every customer.

Feed the roadmap

Bring precise, prioritized field feedback to engineering and the founders: what customers need, what blocks adoption, and what wins deals.
Reproduce customer issues and work with engineering until they ship a fix.

What a typical week looks like

Two days on active pilots: on-site or remote in a prospect's cluster, installing, debugging, and pulling results.
A day on deal calls: discovery, technical deep dives, security reviews, and results readouts.
A day building: an integration a prospect needs, a better install path, or a demo environment.
A day with the team: engineering sync on field feedback, GTM sync on pipeline, and founder time on what we learned.
[Roughly X percent travel] for on-site deployments and customer visits.

You may be a good fit if you have

A strong engineering background: [2–5] years as a software, infrastructure, or ML engineer. You write production-quality code (Python required; Go or Rust a plus).
Hands-on infra experience: you have run or debugged workloads on Kubernetes, Slurm, or Ray, and you are comfortable on Linux, in cloud and on-prem environments.
Customer-facing technical experience: as an FDE, solutions engineer, sales engineer, or similar. You have taken a customer from a blank page to a working result.
Clear communication: you can explain a technical result to an engineer in the morning and to a VP in the afternoon.
Ownership under ambiguity: you drive a deployment to the finish line without a detailed spec or someone checking in.

Strong pluses

Experience with GPU clusters and distributed training (PyTorch, DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron, or similar).
Experience with observability and telemetry (Prometheus, Grafana, DCGM, OpenTelemetry).
Experience at an AI infra, MLOps, or developer-tools company with an enterprise sales motion.
Experience with enterprise security reviews and on-prem software deployments.
Startup or founder experience.

Reasons to take this job

You work on the most compute-intensive workloads in the industry, inside the clusters of the teams that run them.
You see the direct impact of your work: every pilot you run is a deal that closes or doesn't.
Your feedback goes straight into the roadmap, with no layers between you and the founders who built post-training infra at Llama scale.
You build the FDE function from 0 to 1, with a clear path to leading it as it grows.
Great vibe: a strong (and fun) team who worked at the frontier before, substantial GPU capacity to test ideas, and real customers to build with.

Reasons to not take this job

You want to work only on the core product, not inside customer environments.
You don't want to be on calls with customers, or to travel for on-site deployments.
You want a narrow scope. This role moves between engineering, deals, and product every week.
You want a playbook. There isn't one yet.

Location, visa sponsorship & benefits

Hybrid in Palo Alto: 4+ days/week in office.
Visa sponsorship: H-1B and OPT/CPT support available, with immigration counsel.
Meals & perks: Complimentary lunch, dinner, snacks, and drinks.

How to apply

Send us 2 links or short write-ups to start:
something you built or deployed in a customer environment, and a technical problem you solved under real constraints (limited access, a deadline, an unhappy customer). If you can't share details, tell us in a paragraph how you would run a 2-week Goaly pilot on a prospect's 500-GPU cluster.

A note on qualifications.
We value exceptional ability over perfect keyword matches. If the work excites you and you can show strong technical ability, customer instinct, and ownership, we encourage you to apply.

Equal opportunity

We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates who need them during the hiring process.

About The Company

America is under sustained cyber attack. Our adversaries infiltrate our networks, steal our IP, and degrade the digital infrastructure that modern life runs on. They’ve learned—correctly—that those attacks rarely produce consequences.

Twenty was founded to change that, by making our adversaries think twice before they attack us. Our vision is American and allied primacy in cyberspace—a future where they cannot contest us, deterrence is assured, and the free world remains secure.

Founded in 2024, Twenty Technologies (www.twenty.io) industrializes offensive cyber operations for the U.S. and its allies. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Twenty has raised $168M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Caffeinated Capital, Friends & Family Capital, Point72 Ventures, General Catalyst, and In-Q-Tel.

Mission | On Site
| Full Time | Active TS/SCI with Full Scope Polygraph

Role Summary

You'll be on the ground at a government customer site, serving as a generalist engineering presence for Twenty's mission-critical platform in a restricted, air-gapped environment. Twenty builds software for cyber operations, and the applications you'll extend and operate are used by operators and analysts working against hard national security problems.

This is the broadest engineering role at Twenty. In a given month you might build a customer-specific feature, integrate a new data source, get an extension through the customer's deployment process, chase down a production failure, tune the monitoring that would have caught it sooner, and prototype an AI-backed capability with support from Arlington. You won't be an expert in all of it, and the role isn't designed to require that. For specialist work like data engineering and AI engineering, you'll deliver with guidance from the Arlington engineers who specialize in it. What the role does require is range: the ability to pick up an unfamiliar part of the system, get productive quickly, and produce work that holds up in production.

The office-based team can't access this environment, so you are the engineering presence where the software actually runs. Problems reach you first, and the judgment calls are yours: what's wrong, what's urgent, and what Arlington needs to know. When customer work is quiet, you'll build features for Twenty's core product applications, carrying what you learned in the field directly into the product.

You'll report directly to the VP of Engineering. You'll be part of a small forward deployed team, working closely with other on-site colleagues, the Arlington-based product engineering and DevSecOps teams, and the customer's own technical staff.

If you're a strong generalist who wants your work in the hands of operators the same day you build it, and you'd rather own a production system end to end than ship features into a backlog, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

Customer-Specific Features & Extensions

Design and build features, extensions, and integrations that adapt Twenty's applications to this customer's mission, workflows, and environment.
Work directly with customer users and technical staff to understand what they actually need, then scope and deliver it, making pragmatic trade-offs between speed, robustness, and what the environment allows.
Write code that is testable, debuggable, and maintainable by engineers who can't access the environment in which it runs. Tests carry unusual weight here: they're how Arlington trusts a change they'll never see run.
Write code that meets the security standards of classified environments: no hardcoded secrets, disciplined credential handling, and audit-ready practices throughout, so your work moves through the customer's approval process without friction.

Data Integration & AI-Backed Capabilities

Build software extensions that retrieve, parse, transform, and load new data sources into Twenty's applications, working with forward deployed data engineers where present and Arlington data engineers where not.
Investigate unfamiliar source systems and data formats, working with customer stakeholders to understand semantics, access patterns, and constraints before writing code.
Extend and field-test AI-backed capabilities in Twenty's applications with guidance from Arlington AI engineers, and report back what actually works against real data and real users.

Deployment & Site Reliability

Work with the customer's deployment team to get software approved, deployed, and running in the high-side environment, and execute deployments and updates in coordination with Arlington engineering.
Monitor the health of the platform and its data flows on-site using the LGTM stack (Grafana, Loki, Tempo, Mimir); identify anomalies and degradations before they become incidents. In an air-gapped environment, efficiency compounds.
Diagnose and resolve production issues where they happen, escalating to Arlington with a clear picture of what you found, not just what triggered the alert.
Drive root cause analysis and post-incident reviews in partnership with the Arlington engineering team, and turn findings into runbooks, fixes, or upstream design changes.
Participate in on-call rotation using PagerDuty, with clear escalation paths to the engineering team. The environment is air-gapped, so off-hours incident response may require returning to the customer facility rather than remoting in.

Product Engineering

When customer-driven work is quiet, build feature capabilities for Twenty's core product applications alongside the Arlington product engineering teams.
Surface patterns from the field that should become platform capabilities, and advocate for them with the product engineering team. What you generalize from one customer makes every deployment after it faster.

Customer & Team Liaison

Serve as a consistent engineering presence for the government customer: professional, reliable, and clear under pressure.
Relay operational observations, capability gaps, and customer feedback to the Arlington team accurately and promptly.
Work alongside other forward deployed engineers and analysts, sharing context and coverage across the on-site team.

Who You Are

You independently identify the right solution to ambiguous, open-ended problems. Problems reach you before they're fully defined, and the environment's constraints are discovered, not documented; you investigate, form a design, and deliver without waiting for a spec.
You have real range. You've shipped across more of the stack than your title suggests, and you get productive in unfamiliar systems quickly. You'd rather be effective at many things than perfect at one.
You know the difference between what you can do alone and what you should do with help, and you actively use Arlington specialists as a resource without being dependent on them for every decision.
You respond with urgency to operational issues and own resolution within your sphere. You're unafraid to call an incident when the signal warrants it.
You proactively create and update runbooks and documentation for the components you own. In an environment the rest of the team can't access, what you write down is what they know.
You understand the customer and the mission well enough to know which work has the greatest impact, and you redirect your focus when what you're doing isn't moving the needle.
You tailor your communication to your audience, whether that's a product engineer in Arlington, a DevSecOps teammate, or a non-technical customer stakeholder, and you proactively share information so the right people stay informed and aligned.
You're comfortable operating in secure environments where tooling is limited, internet access is not a given, and the stakes are real.

Must Have

Demonstrated range: you've delivered production work outside your core specialty, such as data pipelines, integrations, infrastructure, or ML-backed features, and you're comfortable doing so with support from specialists.
Experience in a forward deployed, field engineering, or embedded customer-facing engineering role, including deploying and operating software in air-gapped, classified, or otherwise restricted environments, with demonstrated ability to work independently and sound judgment about when to decide and when to escalate.
Ability to work on-site full-time at a government facility in Northern Virginia, with travel to Arlington, VA (typically 4 days per month).

Nice to Have

Hands-on experience building ETL/ELT pipelines or data integrations (example technologies: Airflow, NiFi, AWS Glue, or equivalent custom pipeline development), and solid SQL and schema design skills.
Experience building LLM-backed application features or operating AI/ML systems in production.
Hands-on experience with observability tooling (Grafana, Datadog, Splunk, or similar).
Experience with streaming and message queue technologies (example technologies: Kafka, NATS, Kinesis, RabbitMQ).
Background in a military, intelligence, or defense contracting environment.

Security / Work Environment

This role requires an active security clearance
. Work is performed on-site at a government facility, with travel to Twenty's Arlington, VA office typically 4 days per month. Access to systems is restricted and tooling constraints apply.

vCluster is gaining rapid traction with GPU AI Clouds and enterprises building AI Factories: organizations that need to offer Kubernetes as a managed service on bare metal GPU infrastructure, and need to do it fast. This role exists to make that happen.

Strategic Partnering: Join Sales in the pre-sales process where deep infrastructure work is required to achieve a meaningful proof of value.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

Production K8s Mastery: 5+ years of experience deploying and operating Kubernetes in production, ideally on bare metal or in high-complexity environments.
GPU Fluency: Practical knowledge of NVIDIA GPU Operators, CUDA tooling, and systems-level configuration for GPU nodes.
Networking Fundamentals: Deep understanding of CNI plugins, overlay networks, load balancing, and connectivity diagnosis in layered environments.
Storage Expertise: Experience with persistent volume configuration, CSI drivers, and distributed systems like Ceph, Rook, Weka, or Longhorn.

Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

added.title: Applied AI Engineer
added.description:
About The Company

America is under sustained cyber attack. Our adversaries infiltrate our networks, steal our IP, and degrade the digital infrastructure that modern life runs on. They’ve learned—correctly—that those attacks rarely produce consequences.

Twenty was founded to change that, by making our adversaries think twice before they attack us. Our vision is American and allied primacy in cyberspace—a future where they cannot contest us, deterrence is assured, and the free world remains secure.

Founded in 2024, Twenty Technologies (www.twenty.io) industrializes offensive cyber operations for the U.S. and its allies. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Twenty has raised $168M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Caffeinated Capital, Friends & Family Capital, Point72 Ventures, General Catalyst, and In-Q-Tel.

Mission | On Site
| Full Time | U.S. Citizenship Required / No Active Clearance Required

Role Summary

You’ll build an agent environment at Twenty, with an interaction model similar to Claude Code and Codex. Users will give it tasks, supply context, and review its work. They’ll need to see what it’s doing and be able to intervene when it gets something wrong.

Your work will center on the agent harness
: the code that assembles context, executes tool calls, tracks progress, and coordinates delegated work. You’ll decide how information carries across a session, how the agent checks its results, and how it recovers when a step fails.

You’ll write production software in Python, TypeScript, or Rust and maintain it after launch. Expect to spend time investigating failed runs, testing changes to the harness, and working with users to understand where the system needs improvement.

What You’ll Do

Build agent harnesses. Write the execution loop that calls the model, runs tools, records results, and determines the next step. Set time and cost limits. Define stopping conditions and detect runs that repeat work without making progress.
Manage context. Choose what the model sees at each step, including instructions, retrieved records, previous actions, and tool results. Build retrieval and summarization into the workflow. Check that summaries preserve task requirements, source references, and unfinished work. Investigate failures caused by missing information or conflicting instructions.
Orchestrate workflows. Combine model calls with application code and human review. Implement branching, parallel execution, and checkpoints where the task requires them. Store task state so work can resume after an interruption. For delegated work, define what each agent receives, what it returns, and how shared state is updated.
Build tool interfaces. Define inputs, outputs, and error responses. Validate arguments before execution and check results before passing them to the next step. Handle retries so a lost response doesn’t cause duplicate writes or messages.
Build the controls people need to work with an agent. Show progress and make tool calls and results inspectable. Let users correct instructions, approve actions, stop a run, and resume unfinished work. Make clear what has completed, what failed, and what still needs review.
Handle failures and control access. Detect invalid tool calls, dropped requirements, and reports of success that don’t match the actual result. Implement retry limits, cancellation, and escalation to a person. Enforce permissions in application code and require approval for actions that need review.
Evaluate changes. Build test cases from representative tasks and production failures. Check results against the task’s requirements. Measure completion rate, failure severity, human intervention, latency, and cost. Run regression tests when changing models, prompts, tools, retrieval, or orchestration.
Operate the system. Keep traces that show what the model saw, which tools ran, and how task state changed. Redact secrets and restrict access to sensitive traces. Version prompts and workflow code, test releases on a limited set of traffic, and support rollback.

Who You Are

You investigate a failed run before proposing a fix. You’re comfortable reading backend code and tracing a problem through several services. You can explain why you chose an approach, show the results of testing it, and describe what remains uncertain.

You work directly with domain experts to understand the task and its failure cases. You ask which errors are tolerable, which require review, and what a user needs to see before accepting a result.

Must Have

Production software experience. At least four years building and maintaining production software, including hands-on work on an LLM application that calls tools or performs multi-step tasks. Be prepared to discuss failures you encountered after launch and how you addressed them.
Programming and backend engineering skills. Strong production experience in at least one of Python, TypeScript, or Rust, with the ability to work in the others as needed. You can build services, work with asynchronous execution and external APIs, manage persistent storage, and write automated tests.
Harness and orchestration experience. You’ve written or substantially changed an agent’s execution loop. You can explain what the model controls, what the application enforces, and when the user needs to make a decision. You’ve investigated failures involving tool use, lost context, or work that stopped before the task was complete.
Context engineering experience. You’ve worked on retrieval, context assembly, summarization, or memory for an LLM application. You can explain how you chose the information supplied to the model, worked within token limits, and tested whether the right information survived across steps.
Experience handling partial failure. You understand timeouts, retries, concurrency, and idempotency. You can design recovery for a workflow that fails halfway through and verify whether an action completed before attempting it again.
Evaluation and debugging experience. You’ve built tests for model-driven workflows and used execution traces to investigate failures. You can choose checks suited to the task, account for variation between runs, and compare automated grading with human assessments.
Security knowledge. You understand prompt injection and the risks of instructions embedded in retrieved documents or tool output. You can restrict tool access, protect credentials, and implement validation and approval steps for actions such as deleting records, exporting data, or sending messages.

Nice to Have

Experience with long-running or multi-agent workflows, including checkpoint recovery, task delegation, and shared state.
Experience building retrieval or memory systems with source tracking, freshness checks, and access controls that follow the requesting user’s permissions.
Experience running controlled comparisons or ablation studies to measure how individual components affect results.
Experience with self-hosted inference, inference optimization, or task-specific fine-tuning, including measuring their effect on task performance and operating cost.

Tech Environment (You Might Work With)

Python, TypeScript, Rust, model APIs and SDKs, relational databases, object storage, search systems, asynchronous workers, workflow engines, containers, and tracing and evaluation tools.

The implementation may include an orchestration framework or a custom harness. Be prepared to read and debug the execution code, including framework code the application depends on.

Salient builds AI agents for regulated financial services. Our agents automate loan servicing, compliance, collections, recovery, insurance claims, and disputes for banks, captives, and specialty lenders.

Building together in person in San Francisco

We’re looking for a Member of Technical Staff to help build the speech and language models behind Salient’s production voice agents.

You’ll work on challenging problems in speech and language modeling. Many of these problems look solved in academic benchmarks, but remain deeply unsolved in real-world production.

Experience with speech modeling, or LLM post-training.

.

The opportunity

At Unity, we’re shaping the future of real-time 3D development by enabling creators to harness intelligent, autonomous systems. Our next-generation agentic AI - goal-directed, adaptive, and capable of reasoning and planning in dynamic environments - is transforming how games and simulations come to life.

We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to develop these foundational AI systems within the Unity engine, empowering creators to build better games. Your work will directly drive innovation, allowing developers and designers to integrate sophisticated AI behavior seamlessly into their worlds. You’ll also apply data-driven AI to game tuning, using gameplay data and simulation to help creators balance their games and improve the player experience.

This role is perfect for someone passionate about pushing the boundaries of AI, and agentic systems, and intelligent decision-making in complex, real-time environments.

What You'll Be Doing

Design, implement, and scale AI agents that assist in generating game code and executing goal-directed behaviors.
Define orchestration logic for single- and multi-agent systems
Develop reusable agentic frameworks - planning modules, memory systems, or policy adaptation layers - for creator extensibility.
Lead high-impact initiatives, including AI training for scalable behaviors, AI planning and goal inference frameworks, and agent memory and world modeling systems for persistent, believable behavior.
Build data-driven AI solutions for game tuning, using player telemetry, simulated playtesting, and automated playtesting agents to analyze and improve difficulty, pacing, game economy, and level balance.
Develop models that predict player engagement, frustration, and churn from gameplay data, and turn those predictions into concrete tuning recommendations for designers.
Develop recursive self-improvement in agentic systems.
Collaborate across internal and external teams to unlock innovative use cases in gaming, simulation, and interactive storytelling.
Contribute to the long-term vision and roadmap for Unity’s agentic AI offerings, ensuring modularity, usability, and performance across platforms.
Establish and champion best practices for model quality, simulation-based evaluation, and ML/AI safety within real-time systems.

What We're Looking For

Advanced degree (MS or Ph.D.) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field.
3+ years (1+ year with Ph.D.) of hands-on experience developing ML systems in production, ideally within real-time or interactive environments.
Experience with agentic systems, orchestration, or AI tool integration.
Strong background in one or more of the following: LLM training and evaluation, decision-making under uncertainty, AI planning, or agentic systems.
Experience applying data-driven methods such as player modeling, Bayesian optimization, simulation-based evaluation, or causal inference to tune and optimize complex systems.
Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language (e.g., Python, C++, Go, Java) and familiarity with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow).
Strong system design skills and the ability to architect performant, scalable ML systems.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills; ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams including engine developers, designers, and product managers.
Proficient with AI toolings.

You Might Also Have

Familiarity with game development workflows.
Experience with game analytics, player telemetry, live-ops tuning, or A/B testing of game features.
Publications or open-source contributions in modeling, agent-based modeling, or related areas.
Experience with behavior trees, utility AI, or hierarchical task planning.
Passion for the gaming industry and AI applications in games.

Your ability to influence decisions at the C-suite level, while maintaining hands-on technical credibility, is what sets you apart. Lead FDE pods of 2-5 onshore anchored and offshore supported engineers, owning execution, resource management, escalations and overall delivery health

Set direction for prompt engineering, tool-use patterns, and human-in-the-loop controls
Govern end-to-end RAG pipeline design-including ingestion, chunking, embedding, vector retrieval, and hybrid search-ensuring production-grade quality and scalability.

Engineering & Data Foundations

Review and contribute to production-quality code
Guide architecture of data pipelines powering GenAI use cases

Deep familiarity with cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and/or Google Cloud)

added.title: Senior Expert Data Scientist, Human Genetics
added.description:
Summary

Location: Cambridge

This position is located in Cambridge, MA and does not have the ability to be located remotely. Please only apply if this area is accessible to you.

We are seeking a highly motivated computational scientist to join the Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disease (CVM) research organization at Biomedical

Research (BR) in Cambridge, MA. In this role, you will apply human genetics, statistical genetics, and genomic data science to support new therapeutic target discovery and patient selection strategies across CVM diseases.

The successful candidate will work closely with geneticists, computational biologists, disease-area scientists, translational researchers, and clinical development colleagues to generate actionable insights from human genetic and genomic data. This is an opportunity to contribute to innovative drug discovery programs and help advance genetically informed approaches to precision medicine.

About The Role

Key Responsibilities

Analyze and interpret whole exome/genome sequencing data to identify genetic variants, genes, and biological pathways associated with cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.
Develop and apply statistical genetics and bioinformatics methods for variant annotation, association analysis, burden testing, rare-variant analysis, causal inference, and gene prioritization.
Support the identification, evaluation, and validation of novel therapeutic targets using human genetic evidence and complementary genomic data sources.
Contribute to patient selection and stratification strategies for research and clinical programs, including the identification of genetically defined patient subgroups.
Integrate human genetics results with transcriptomic, proteomic, functional genomics, clinical, and other relevant data to develop disease and target insights.
Collaborate with cross-functional project teams to define analytical strategies, interpret findings, and translate results into clear scientific recommendations.
Develop reproducible, well-documented analytical workflows and contribute to best practices for genomic data analysis.
Communicate results through presentations, written reports, scientific manuscripts, and internal project updates.
Stay current with advances in human genetics, statistical genetics, genomic medicine, and computational methods relevant to drug discovery and development.

Essential Requirements

PhD with 2-3+ years or MS with 6+ years of industry experience in human genetics, statistical genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, epidemiology, biostatistics, or a related field.
Postdoctoral research experience is preferred.
Demonstrated experience analyzing whole exome/genome sequencing data, including variant quality control, annotation, filtering, association testing, and interpretation.
Strong understanding of human genetics and statistical genetics principles, including rare-variant analysis and genotype-phenotype associations.
Familiarity with genome-wide association studies, phenome-wide association studies, polygenic risk scores, Mendelian randomization, or functional genomics.
Experience integrating genomic data with clinical, molecular, or multi-omic datasets.
Programming and data analysis expertise in Python or R, along with proficiency in Linux or Unix-based computing environments.
Knowledge of workflow management systems (Git), collaborative coding, and reproducible research practices.
Ability to work with large-scale genomic datasets and use appropriate statistical and computational methods to derive biologically meaningful conclusions.
Strong scientific communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience applying human genetic evidence to target discovery, target validation, or drug development.

The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and

experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published

salary range based on company and market factors.

role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards.

disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.

About The Job

The People and AI Research (PAIR) team conducts foundational research to make human-AI partnerships productive, enjoyable, and fair. Based in Cambridge, MA, our multidisciplinary team of computer scientists, research engineers, social scientists, and designers invents novel interaction paradigms and develops open-source tools that shape how people interact with intelligent systems.

As a Research Scientist in Human-AI Interaction and Simulation, you will develop computational, cognitive, and statistical models of human behavior to understand, predict, and optimize how people interact with advanced AI systems. Generative models, multimodal assistants, and autonomous agents are transforming interactive computing. Designing effective human-AI partnerships requires models of human cognitive limits, trust dynamics, steerability, and collaboration patterns.

In this role, you will design empirical user studies, build predictive simulations of user interaction, and translate behavioral insights into architectural and UX improvements across Google DeepMind's frontier models.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Develop, validate, and land models of human behavior in the context of human-AI interactions, translating complex behavioral insights into actionable improvements for frontier AI models, interactive tools, and user interfaces.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Job Description

The Solution Architect is able to lead a workstream in sophisticated enterprise customer engagements, partnering with key collaborators to drive and achieve the vision while completing key deliverables. The Sr. Solution Architect leads one or more workstreams in sophisticated enterprise customer engagements, partnering with key collaborators to drive and achieve the vision while completing key deliverables. They serve as hands-on advisors, using strong communication skills, solution and/or technical knowledge, Salesforce product knowledge, industry experience, consulting experience, and knowledge of their client’s business to deliver customer return on investment.

They are proficient at analyzing issues and obstacles to resolve root cause, and can identify appropriate corrective action. On a day to day basis, they interact with customer product owner, business process owner and technical resources to understand requirements, analyze information, and craft comprehensive solutions. Solution Architects are stewards of the Professional Services Methodology.
